newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia crudes up on Iraq, paper Tapis trade flurry.
newsitem.headline: Asia crudes up on Iraq, paper Tapis trade flurry.

text.p: Asian crude prices were mostly firmer on Thursday, supported by increased tensions between Iraq and the United States.
The Brent/Dubai spread widened in response to an overnight Brent futures rally, which continued in Asian hours on Thursday.
The November Brent/Dubai was bid at $2.10 per barrel and a notional offer placed at $2.20, about 25 cents wider than the day-earlier levels and about 15 cents out from London's late quotes.
A November Brent/Dubai traded on Wednesday as high as $2.11 between a U.S. refiner and a U.S. trader.
Earlier in the week a south European state oil company and a trader exchanged November Brent and December Dubai at $2.40.
Dubai intermonth spreads were steady however, with November/December and December/January quoted at 39/45 cents.
Front-month Brent traded as high as $23.80 on SIMEX, a post Gulf War high, although it traded higher at $23.82 in London overnight after Iraq fired a surface to air missile at U.S. jets.
Paper Tapis rose about 25 cents per barrel and sparked a flurry of trades at $22.50 on October covering more than 250,000 barrels.
A European major and a U.S. refiner were noted sellers around that level. A European trader was noted on the buy side.
Traders said they expected three Tapis physical cargoes to be available for October's spot market.
Talk of trades of a November Umm Shaif and a November Lower Zakum, both said done at ADNOC plus 30 cents, were denied by the parties said to have been involved.
Wet trading talk was quiet, as players waited for the Nov MidEast market and the Oct regional market to wind up.
Indonesia allocations are expected by early next week.
